newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off in lackluster trade.

text.p: NYMEX crude slipped in lackluster trading Tuesday as traders shrugged off expectations for this evening's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) as predictably following seasonal trends.

"I am not sure these stats will have much of an effect. They are seasonal in that demand for gasoline now is poor so it's (stocks are) supposed to build, while winter demand for heat is causing a (distillate) draw," said Michael Busby, trader with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.
March crude settled off four cents at $23.90 a barrel.
February heating oil and gasoline both finished lower as dealers rolled positions into the March contract ahead of the February contract expiry for refined products on Friday.
Feb heat ended off 0.46 cent at 66.83 cents a gallon. Feb gasoline ended off 0.58 cent at 67.04 cents a gallon.
A consensus of trader estimates for the API data called for a two million barrel draw in distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel.
Gasoline and crude stocks were expected to build by 2.25 million and three million barrels respectively.
The data reflects the week ended January 24.
Due to the seasonality of the API expectations, dealers said the estimates were already reflected in oil prices.
Still, traders said a spate of refinery maintenance has created uncertainty about how much output had declined last week.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
